chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The intensely dyed (vibrant-colored) garment is disliked, except for the bride/groom.

key_terms.الْعَرُوسِ: The bride or groom; refers to the wedding context
key_terms.الْمُفْدَمُ: Intensely dyed garment; specifically refers to deep red or vividly saturated dye
key_terms.يُكْرَهُ: Is disliked/makruh; a jurisprudential category of discouraged but not forbidden actions

ai.seo_question: Is wearing brightly colored clothes haram in Islam according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) issues a legal ruling that wearing intensely or vividly dyed clothing (al-mufdam) is disapproved (makruh) in Islamic jurisprudence, with the exception of wedding attire. The term 'al-mufdam' refers specifically to garments dyed to a deep, saturated red or similarly vibrant hue. This exception acknowledges the legitimacy of celebration and adornment in the context of marriage, balancing the general principle of modest dress with the festive occasion of a wedding.
